title_en: Measures for the Administration of Foreign Vessels on Border Rivers

articles.content_en: These Measures are formulated for the purposes of safeguarding the sovereignty of the People's Republic of China, facilitating the entry and exit of foreign vessels into and out of the ports on the boundary rivers between China and neighboring countries (hereinafter referred to as "ports on boundary rivers") and the rivers connecting China and neighboring countries (hereinafter referred to as "connecting rivers with neighboring countries"), and ensuring navigation safety of foreign vessels.
All foreign vessels entering or leaving the ports on boundary rivers and the connecting rivers with neighboring countries shall comply with these Measures.

In the ports on boundary rivers and the ports of the connecting rivers with neighboring countries, the Harbour Superintendency of the People's Republic of China shall be established.
The Harbour Superintendency shall be responsible for supervising the implementation and enforcement of these Measures and relevant navigation laws and regulations; examining and approving applications for the entry and exit of foreign vessels; implementing compulsory pilotage for foreign vessels permitted to enter or leave and organizing joint inspections; supervising the technical condition of foreign vessels entering or leaving and maintaining navigation safety and order; investigating and handling maritime accidents involving foreign vessels entering or leaving.

Foreign vessels may enter or leave the ports on boundary rivers and the connecting rivers with neighboring countries only in accordance with the agreement on merchant ship navigation signed between the government of their flag state and the Chinese government, or upon obtaining permission from the Chinese government; for each entry or exit, they must also report to the Harbour Superintendency for approval in accordance with Article 5 and paragraph 2 of Article 9 of these Measures.

When a foreign vessel intends to enter a port on a boundary river or a connecting river with a neighboring country, the master, before the vessel's departure from the port of departure, shall report to the Harbour Superintendency of the intended port of arrival on the boundary river or the first port of the connecting river with a neighboring country for approval, through the vessel's agent in the port, the name of the vessel, the number of vessels in the fleet, the maximum draft, the names and quantities of cargo, the number of passengers carried, and the scheduled time of arrival at the joint inspection (pilotage) anchorage of the port on the boundary river or the connecting river with a neighboring country. If the port of departure of the foreign vessel is on the opposite bank of the intended port of arrival on the boundary river, the formalities may be simplified by reporting for approval with signals prescribed by the Harbour Superintendency.

Foreign vessels, when entering or leaving the ports on boundary rivers and navigating in the connecting rivers with neighboring countries, shall fly various prescribed signal flags, and during the daytime shall also fly the national flag of their flag state; when navigating in the connecting rivers with neighboring countries, they shall also fly the national flag of the People's Republic of China at the top of the foremast.

Foreign vessels, when entering or leaving the ports on boundary rivers and the connecting rivers with neighboring countries, must apply to the Harbour Superintendency for pilotage by a pilot. During the period of berthing in the port, a foreign vessel shall not move berth without being piloted by a pilot. If, due to special circumstances, the pilotage anchorage has not been designated in a port on a boundary river, the Harbour Superintendency may waive the pilotage application for foreign vessels entering or leaving.

When a foreign vessel enters the pilotage anchorage, the master shall declare to the Harbour Superintendency the names and quantities of all weapons, ammunition, radio transmitters, radiotelephone transmitters, radar, rocket signals, signal guns, etc. on board, and shall comply with the following provisions:
(1) Weapons and ammunition shall be sealed up by the Harbour Superintendency;
(2) Radio transmitters, radiotelephone transmitters, radar, rocket signals, signal guns, etc. shall be prohibited from use.
In the event of distress or accident, the vessel may use the items listed in subparagraph (2) of the preceding paragraph, but shall immediately report to the Harbour Superintendency after such use.

When a foreign vessel enters the pilotage anchorage, the master shall fill in the forms prescribed by the Harbour Superintendency, submit relevant ship documents for inspection, and accept the joint inspection by the Harbour Superintendency and relevant authorities.
For the departure of a foreign vessel, the master shall report to the Harbour Superintendency for approval through the vessel's agent in the port, then fill in the prescribed forms, undergo joint inspection, and may only depart after the Harbour Superintendency issues an exit permit.

When foreign vessels are navigating in the connecting rivers with neighboring countries, the Harbour Superintendency or other relevant inspection authorities may dispatch personnel to work on board, and the master shall provide convenience.

Foreign vessels are prohibited from berthing, anchoring, embarking or disembarking persons, and loading or discharging cargo at places on the Chinese bank of the boundary river or in the connecting river with a neighboring country that have not been designated. In the event of a maritime accident or force majeure, exceptions may be made, but the master shall immediately report to the Harbour Superintendency or the local People's Committee.

When a maritime accident occurs to a foreign vessel in a port on a boundary river or a connecting river with a neighboring country, the master shall promptly submit a report on the maritime accident to the Harbour Superintendency and await investigation and handling by the Harbour Superintendency.

Where a foreign vessel, its crew members or passengers violate these Measures or relevant navigation laws and regulations, the Harbour Superintendency shall, based on the circumstances, handle the matter.

Where the government of the flag state of a foreign vessel has signed an agreement on merchant ship navigation with the Chinese government, the provisions of the agreement shall still be implemented; matters not provided for in the agreement shall be implemented in accordance with these Measures.

The People's Committees of the relevant provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, in accordance with these Measures and in light of local specific conditions, formulate implementing rules.
These Measures are approved by the State Council and shall be promulgated and come into force by the Ministry of Communications.
